technical.lead: Microsoft Build ships in-house MAI models, multi-model Foundry, Agent 365
technical.body: Satya Nadella opened Microsoft Build 2026 at Fort Mason Center in San Francisco this morning with agents as the throughline and shipping artifacts rather than a roadmap. The clearest net-new piece is an in-house MAI model family debuting on stage — including a coding-focused model positioned to power GitHub Copilot alongside speech, voice, and image models — Microsoft's most explicit move yet to reduce its foundation-model dependence on OpenAI, per [FAQ - Microsoft Build 2026: the MAI model family that signals the end of OpenAI dependency](https://faq.com.tw/en/developer-tools/2026-06-01-microsoft-build-2026-mai-coding-models-en/). Azure AI Foundry is the orchestration layer underneath: its marketplace now spans 3,000+ models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Llama, Mistral, and specialty providers, and Microsoft is rebuilding Copilot orchestration so Claude runs as a first-class alternative to GPT in the same environment — Azure positions itself as the only cloud offering both Claude and GPT frontier models on one platform, with Claude usable through Anthropic's Claude Code agent, per [Microsoft Azure Blog - Introducing Anthropic's Claude models in Microsoft Foundry](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/introducing-anthropics-claude-models-in-microsoft-foundry-bringing-frontier-intelligence-to-azure/). Two named grounding-and-governance components anchor the agent stack: Work IQ, the intelligence layer that lets a Foundry agent delegate natural-language tasks against a user's Microsoft 365 mail, meetings, files, and chats over the Agent-to-Agent protocol while enforcing the signed-in user's permissions and sensitivity labels (public preview, Microsoft 365 Copilot license required), per [Microsoft Learn - Connect agents to Microsoft 365 with Work IQ (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/work-iq); and Agent 365, the enterprise control plane that monitors agent decisions, tracks accuracy over time, and enforces compliance boundaries, paired with Office 365 Copilot Agent Mode and a GitHub Copilot pushed from pair programmer toward an autonomous agent assigned bugs, features, and pull requests, per [Windows Forum - Build 2026: Microsoft makes AI agents the new work model](https://windowsforum.com/threads/build-2026-microsoft-makes-ai-agents-the-new-work-model-agent-mode-agent-365-local-ai.421349/).

technical.lead: Snowflake wires Claude into Cortex AI, ships agent control plane
technical.body: At the Snowflake Summit 26 Platform Keynote this morning — Benoit Dageville and Christian Kleinerman in the 9:00 AM PT Tuesday slot — the headline announcement is that Snowflake will integrate Anthropic's Claude directly into Cortex AI, extending the roughly $200M partnership the two signed in December and letting Snowflake's 13,900+ enterprise customers run Claude-powered agents against governed data without that data leaving the platform — framed as the answer for finance, healthcare, and public-sector teams wary of data leakage. Daniela Amodei argued on stage that "building security and customer trust can be an accelerant that speeds up business," and Snowflake named early adopters: Carvana applying AI across inventory, logistics, finance, and demand management; eSentire applying Claude to threat detection and investigation; and Notion building an agent that connects directly to Snowflake data, per [Seoul Economic Daily - Snowflake integrates Anthropic's Claude into its platform](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/06/02/snowflake-integrates-anthropics-claude-into-its-platform). The agentic control plane is organized around two named pieces — Snowflake Intelligence, a natural-language work agent for knowledge workers exploring governed data, and Cortex Code ("Coco"), an AI coding agent for developers and data engineers — sitting alongside a broader roadmap reveal of Openflow ingestion, Adaptive Compute, Cortex AISQL, and agentic listings on the Snowflake Marketplace, per the [cData - Snowflake Summit 2026 pre-event guide](https://www.cdata.com/blog/snowflake-summit-2026-guide).

technical.lead: BadHost host-header flaw in Starlette hits the LLM serving stack
technical.body: Fresh analysis this week sharpens the blast radius of BadHost (CVE-2026-48710), a host-header injection flaw in the Starlette ASGI framework — the routing core under FastAPI — that lets an attacker control the path a request appears to target by inserting a single character into the HTTP Host header, defeating any path-based authentication middleware. Starlette pulls roughly 325 million downloads a week, and the flaw reaches directly into the local-LLM serving stack: it was found by German security firm X41 D-Sec during an OSTIF-sponsored audit of vLLM, and the affected surface spans FastAPI, vLLM, LiteLLM, and MCP servers — whose spec mandates unauthenticated OAuth discovery endpoints, giving attackers a reliable exploitation path — with researchers chaining the primitive to authentication bypass, server-side request forgery, and in some cases remote code execution against AI services sitting on internal networks without reverse-proxy protection, per [InfoQ - BadHost vulnerability exposes AI agents, evaluators, and LLM gateways](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/06/badhost-ai-systems-vulnerability/). The fix shipped in Starlette 1.0.1 (released May 21, one day ahead of public disclosure), and the practical mitigation is to read the request path from the ASGI scope rather than the reconstructed URL in any middleware that makes a security decision; a free scanner is posted at [BadHost - CVE-2026-48710 Starlette host-header auth bypass](https://badhost.org/). The assigned CVSS score is 6.5, which the disclosing researchers argue understates the downstream impact given how cleanly the single-character primitive escalates, per the [OSTIF - Disclosing the BadHost vulnerability in Starlette](https://ostif.org/disclosing-the-badhost-vulnerability-in-starlette/).

technical.lead: GitHub Copilot flips all plans to usage-based billing
technical.body: GitHub Copilot switched all plans to usage-based billing on June 1, retiring the flat-rate premium-request model: premium request units are replaced by GitHub AI Credits consumed against published per-model token rates for input, output, and cached tokens, and the prior fallback that let users who exhausted their allowance drop to a cheaper model and keep working is gone — usage is now governed by available credits and admin budget controls, per [The GitHub Blog - GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing](https://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/github-copilot-is-moving-to-usage-based-billing/). The change has drawn sustained developer pushback, with users posting projections of 10x-to-50x cost increases — one estimating a jump from $29 to $750 a month, another from $50 to $3,000 — as the metered model exposes heavy agentic workloads to per-token cost, per the [GitHub Community Discussion - GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/192948). The timing lands directly against Microsoft's Build keynote the next morning, where the in-house MAI coding model is pitched as a lower-inference-cost engine for Copilot — the billing shift and the cheaper first-party model are two halves of the same margin story.

technical.lead: Snowflake Summit and Microsoft Build mid-keynote today; WWDC, Databricks ahead
technical.body: The dense San Francisco conference window is at its peak today. Snowflake Summit 26 runs June 1-4 at Moscone Center with 20,000+ attendees, 500+ sessions across 12 tracks, and 190+ partner booths; the Tuesday June 2 Platform Keynote (Dageville and Kleinerman, 9:00 AM PT) is happening now, with a Builder Keynote of live agent demos Wednesday June 3 at 9:00 AM PT still ahead, per [Moscone Center - Snowflake Summit 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/snowflake-summit-2026). Microsoft Build 2026 opened this morning and runs June 2-3 at Fort Mason Center, Nadella's keynote having streamed from 9:30 AM PT, with the in-person cohort capped near 2,500 developers. AI Tinkerers SF hosts its invite-only VIP Dinner: Harnessing Agents tonight June 2 for engineers shipping production agentic systems, per the [AI Tinkerers SF - VIP Dinner: Harnessing Agents](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/p/ai-tinkerers-vip-dinner-harnessing-agents) page, plus an Advanced MCP Showcase sponsored by WorkOS later in the month per the [AI Tinkerers SF - Advanced MCP Showcase](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/p/ai-tinkerers-advanced-mcp-showcase). Apple WWDC26 runs June 8-12 at Apple Park, with the keynote and Platforms State of the Union Monday June 8 (keynote 10:00 AM PT) and 1,000+ developers attending in person by lottery, per [Apple Developer - WWDC26 special event](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/special-event/). Databricks Data + AI Summit runs June 15-18 across Moscone with 800+ sessions spanning data engineering, governance, analytics, applications, and agents, per [Moscone Center - Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/databricks-data-ai-summit-2026). The AI Engineer World's Fair caps the wave at Moscone West, with badge pickup Sunday June 28 and the main program June 29 through July 2 — 29 tracks, 300+ speakers, 100+ expo partners, and 6,000+ attendees, per the [AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026) site.
